name: Mons Mouton
summary: A broad, high massif west of the Nobile–Mouton area. This representative point sits on the summit ridge at 5.85 km, one of the highest terrain points in the south polar region, with a long western horizon.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Mons Mouton Plateau
summary: The gently sloping plateau that hosted Intuitive Machines' IM-2 Athena landing attempt in March 2025. This representative point lies at 5.32 km near 84.79°S, 29.20°E.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · IM-2 · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Nobile Rim 1
summary: A knoll on the eastern rim of Nobile Crater, where elevated terrain catches grazing sunlight. The representative point is 1.85 km above the reference sphere with a 3.0° local slope.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Nobile Rim 2
summary: A flatter, lower bench on the Nobile rim near 84.14°S, 59.72°E. The representative point has a 0.3° local slope, but terrain to the west blocks part of the sky.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Peak near Cabeus B
summary: A 5.68 km massif on the western side of the south polar region, near Cabeus B. High ground improves solar access, but the surrounding terrain creates a deep western horizon.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Malapert Massif
summary: The 5.17 km Malapert Massif, a classic 'peak of eternal light' candidate with near-continuous illumination and a comparatively open horizon toward Earth.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
summary: A rim segment on the western edge of de Gerlache crater, close to the pole. Low local slopes and a narrow skyline make it a compact, accessible benchmark site.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Haworth
summary: A knoll on the northern rim of Haworth crater. Low elevation and a prominent 18° terrain horizon to the north make it a useful contrast case for power and communication risk.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Slater Plain
summary: A broad, low plain near Slater crater at 87.74°S, 115.61°E. Regional slopes are gentle, but a roughly 10° northern horizon limits Sun and Earth visibility.
source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Peak near Shackleton
summary: A 1.18 km ridge point on Shackleton's rim, used as a reference site in the Artemis III site-selection literature. Strong Earth view and long light windows make it a useful baseline.
source: Peña-Asensio et al. (2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Connecting Ridge
summary: The ridge linking Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. Frequently cited as a peak-of-eternal-light candidate; included as a reference for comparing illumination, terrain, and Earth access.
source: Peña-Asensio et al. (2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

name: Shackleton Crater Floor
summary: The permanently shadowed floor of Shackleton crater, 2.75 km below the reference sphere. Included as a volatile-access reference, not as a crewed landing candidate.
